steps.label: (a|0>+b|1>) (x) (c|0>+d|1>) = ac|00>+ad|01>+bc|10>+bd|11>
steps.sub: A product state's 4 amplitudes always fit this [ac,ad,bc,bd] pattern

steps.label: Entangled: a state that provably does NOT fit that pattern
steps.sub: Not just hard to find such a, b, c, d — genuinely unsolvable

caption: A perfectly normal, correctly normalized 2-qubit state — nothing about the vector itself looks unusual.

eyebrow: Trying to Factor It: Always a Contradiction
code:
match [ac,ad,bc,bd] to [1/sqrt2, 0, 0, 1/sqrt2]
ad=0 -> a=0 or d=0

if a=0: ac=0, but ac must be 1/sqrt2 -- contradiction
if d=0: bd=0, but bd must be 1/sqrt2 -- contradiction
caption: Every path leads to a contradiction — there is no a, b, c, d, real or complex, that reproduces this vector. That unsolvability IS entanglement.

steps.label: Nonzero on |00> and |11>, exactly zero on |01> and |10>
steps.sub: Forcing both cross-terms to zero while both diagonal terms stay nonzero breaks factorization

steps.label: Entanglement is a property of the vector, not a signal or force
steps.sub: The proof never mentions distance or time at all
